    "5": {"processing_time": 13, "due_date": 475, "weight": 4},
    "6": {"processing_time": 16, "due_date": 128, "weight": 1},
    "7": {"processing_time": 70, "due_date": 513, "weight": 7},
    "8": {"processing_time": 6, "due_date": 143, "weight": 1},
    "9": {"processing_time": 91, "due_date": 160, "weight": 7},
    "10": {"processing_time": 56, "due_date": 555, "weight": 7},
    "11": {"processing_time": 77, "due_date": 116, "weight": 9},
    "12": {"processing_time": 60, "due_date": 483, "weight": 5},
    "13": {"processing_time": 48, "due_date": 344, "weight": 9},
    "14": {"processing_time": 85, "due_date": 244, "weight": 10}
}

# Create a new model
model = gp.Model("single_machine_scheduling")
model.Params.OutputFlag = 0  # Suppress output

# Sets and parameters
job_ids = list(jobs.keys())
n = len(job_ids)

# Variables
C = model.addVars(job_ids, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="C")  # Completion times
T = model.addVars(job_ids, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="T")  # Tardiness
x = model.addVars(job_ids, job_ids, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")  # Sequencing variables

# Objective: Minimize weighted sum of tardiness
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(jobs[j]["weight"] * T[j] for j in job_ids), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Constraints
M = sum(jobs[j]["processing_time"] for j in job_ids)  # Big M

# Completion time constraints
for j in job_ids:
    model.addConstr(C[j] >= jobs[j]["processing_time"])

# Tardiness constraints
for j in job_ids:
    model.addConstr(T[j] >= C[j] - jobs[j]["due_date"])

# Sequencing constraints
for i in job_ids:
    for j in job_ids:
        if i != j:
            model.addConstr(C[i] + M * x[i, j] <= C[j] + M - jobs[i]["processing_time"])

# Each job must be scheduled exactly once
for j in job_ids:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in job_ids if i != j) == 1)
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[j, i] for i in job_ids if i != j) == 1)

# Optimize model
model.optimize()

# Extract the sequence
sequence = []
for i in job_ids:
    for j in job_ids:
        if i != j and x[i, j].X > 0.5:
            sequence.append((i, j))

# Reconstruct the job order
job_order = []
current_job = next(j for j in job_ids if sum(x[i, j].X for i in job_ids if i != j) == 0)
while len(job_order) < n:
    job_order.append(current_job)
    current_job = next(j for j in job_ids if x[current_job, j].X > 0.5)

# Output the result
result = {
    "sequence": job_order,
    "objective_value": model.ObjVal
}

print(json.dumps(result))
